tools.name: run_select_query
tools.description: Execute a read-only SELECT statement and return up to `max_rows` rows as an array of objects keyed by column name. Rejects INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL with an error — use run_write_query for those. Use this when you need to read data; use describe_table first if you do not know the schema.

sql.description: A single SELECT statement. Must not contain multiple statements or a trailing semicolon followed by more SQL.

max_rows.description: Truncate the result after this many rows.

timeout_ms.description: Abort the query after this many milliseconds.

tools.name: run_write_query
tools.description: Execute a single INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement inside a transaction and commit it. Returns `{ rows_affected }`. Use this instead of run_select_query when you need to mutate data. DDL statements are rejected — use migrate_schema.

sql.description: A single INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statement. Parameter placeholders use `?` with positional values in `params`.

params.description: Values bound to the `?` placeholders, in order.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Return the column definitions for one table: name, type, nullability, default, and primary-key flag. Use this before writing a query if you are unsure of the column names. Returns an array of column descriptors.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List every table in the database with its estimated row count and size in bytes. Returns an array of `{ name, schema, rows, bytes }`. Does not include views — use list_views for those.

include_system.description: Include tables owned by the database engine itself.

tools.name: list_views
tools.description: List every view in the database with the SQL used to define it. Returns an array of `{ name, schema, definition }`. Use this when you need to understand a derived table rather than a physical one.
